chunks: From him, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he assigned liability to the guide, the driver, and the rider, so he said:
Whatever the foot hits, it is upon the driver, and whatever the hand hits, it is upon the guide and the rider.

key_terms.الرِّجْلُ: The foot/leg (specifically hind legs in this context)
key_terms.السَّائِقَ: The driver (one who drives/controls the animal)
key_terms.الْقَائِدَ: The guide (one who leads the animal)
key_terms.الْيَدُ: The hand (specifically front legs in this context)

ai.seo_question: Who is legally responsible for damages caused by an animal's legs in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the specific mechanics of animal liability (daman) by distinguishing between the hind legs, controlled by the driver (sa'iq), and the front limbs, managed by the guide (qa'id) and rider. This classification reflects the Shia juristic understanding of proximate cause, assigning financial responsibility based on which part of the animal inflicted the damage. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how physical control correlates with legal accountability in Islamic tort law.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the guide, and the usher, and the rider is responsible, so he<sup>asws</sup> said:
‘Whatever the (hind) legs hit, so it is upon the usher, and whatever the hands (front legs) hit, so it is upon the guide and the rider’.
